title: Design exercise: SAA-1.3-S01
scenario: Northgate Dental Group stores patient imaging and billing records in 60 S3 buckets across 8 AWS accounts and faces a SOC 2 Type II audit plus a cyber-insurance renewal. The auditor asks for three things: written evidence of what the cloud provider itself is responsible for, continuous proof rather than a yearly screenshot that every bucket stays encrypted and non-public, and confirmation that billing records cannot be deleted or shortened by anyone, administrators included, for seven years. The insurer also wants every bucket labelled by data sensitivity with one consistent set of values, which today drift between accounts. The compliance analyst has no budget for a third-party governance tool.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
No third-party compliance or governance tooling may be purchased
The seven-year retention control must bind account administrators
The labelling standard must be enforced across all 8 accounts rather than by hand

rubric.label: Each of the four asks (provider evidence, continuous proof, seven-year retention, consistent labels) is mapped to a distinct control
The seven-year retention on billing records cannot be shortened or removed by an administrator or the root user

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
